reason: The passage demonstrates Israel's direct reliance on and acknowledgment of Yahweh as the primary source of their victory. Moses serves as Yahweh's instrument, and the Israelites follow his divinely-authorized commands. The text explicitly frames the battle as belonging to God ('the battle is the Lord's against Amalek'), and Israel's success is shown to be contingent upon their connection to the divine (through Moses' raised staff). The building of an altar named 'Yahweh is my banner' (יְהוָה נִסִּי) further demonstrates that the Hebrews consciously orient their actions and identity around their relationship with Yahweh. Their military victory, religious commemoration, and obedience to divinely-guided leadership all illustrate that Yahweh-following is central to their collective action and identity in this foundational narrative.
